It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, ocr scan reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff.

items.title: Intelligence Has a Speed Limit
items.summary: In AI circles, Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) is talked about in almost magical terms: a model tweaks itself, becomes smarter, uses that intellect to rewrite itself again, and this leads to

sourceMetadata.author: @docmilanfar
sourceMetadata.pageDescription: Intelligence Has a Speed Limit In AI circles, Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) is talked about in almost magical terms: a model tweaks itself, becomes smarter, uses that intellect to rewrite itself again, and this leads to super-intelligence. It’s an intuitive and appealing idea. Talk to anyone from control theory though (the discipline that brought you the auto-pilot etc.), and they’ll raise an eyebrow because they know the expectation is naive in a very specific way. We all know self-improvement is impossible. But any self-improving loop has a maximum safe speed, set by how fast you can generate trustworthy evidence that a change was actually an improvement. Control theory’s small-gain theorem says a feedback loop stays stable when the product of its gains stays below one. Gain is a measure of amplification. Here it means how large a modification the system makes per unit of evidence (that the modification helps.) The entire appeal of RSI is high gain: rapid progress.
